Run an action when you attach the pen to the tablet\'s magnetic charger or take it off, for example a Home Assistant webhook. Webhooks get \"gesture\": \"pen_attached\" or \"pen_detached\", broadcasts the extra gesture. Only real changes count: connecting to a pen that\'s already attached doesn\'t.

Double tap the thumb area of the pen to run a shortcut. Double tap twice in a row for the second one, three times for the third, and so on. Drag the handle to reorder, swipe sideways to remove. Choose Nothing to skip a count, for example to run something only on four double taps in a row.

How long the app waits for the next double tap in a row. Shorter feels snappier, longer makes chains easier. Only matters when you have two or more shortcuts.
Send pen events to automation apps

For Tasker, MacroDroid, Automate and similar apps. Besides running your shortcuts, the app sends an Android broadcast for every pen event:
• Double taps: action io.github.ardyln.stylo2.action.DOUBLE_TAP, extras taps (1, 2, 3, …) and gesture (double_tap, double_tap_2, …)
• Charger: action io.github.ardyln.stylo2.action.CHARGER, extras attached (true or false) and gesture (pen_attached, pen_detached)
In your automation app, add an "intent received" trigger with that action. While this is on, a double tap always waits for the full chain time before it runs, so automations can use longer chains.
Tells the Stylo 2 app which app window is focused, so double taps and textures can follow notes apps like Saber. Only the package name of the focused window is read.

Apps other than Saber where the thumb button acts as a stylus button. A double tap presses Android\'s primary stylus button (BUTTON_STYLUS_PRIMARY, the side button on most styluses) and keeps it held; the next double tap releases it. What that does is up to the app: many note apps erase while it\'s held, others select or ignore it. Shortcuts and presentation mode pause in these apps. Saber has its own page.
While one of these apps is open, the pen uses the texture below instead of the main one. There\'s no per-tool integration for these apps, so the same texture applies to all their tools.

Use the pen as a remote and pointer for slides, documents, photos and maps. It uses the touch area near the tip, the same place you double tap. The pointer only moves while a finger is on the touch area, so it stays put when you put the pen down or gesture with it.
The pointer follows every movement of the pen, like a laser pointer. Handy for presenting, but it also moves while you hold the pen otherwise.

How the app tells your touches on the touch area apart:

1. You touch the area and let go. If your finger was there for less than the longest tap, it's a single tap. Otherwise you were holding it to move the pointer, and nothing else happens.
2. Double taps are recognised by the pen itself and reported separately, so they never count as two single taps.

Touch the area to try it: the card below shows how long your last touch was.

Touches up to %1$s count as a tap (single tap: %2$s). Keep your finger on the area longer than that to move the pointer instead. If your taps sometimes don\'t register, move this to the right. If holding sometimes counts as a tap, move it to the left.

A single tap (%2$s) runs %1$s after you let go. The pen reports double taps (%3$s) on its own, so no delay is needed; it\'s only a safeguard in case a double tap ever also runs your single-tap action. Instant is the default.

Instant: a single tap (%1$s) runs the moment you let go. Double taps (%2$s) are reported by the pen on its own and never count as single taps, so no delay is needed. If a double tap ever also runs your single-tap action, add a short delay here.

What the pen, the focused window, Saber and the virtual stylus button report, with what it means

Saber itself is not modified. This app uses an accessibility service to detect when Saber\'s window is focused. With root, it reads Saber\'s settings file to see the active tool, and adds a virtual stylus button that Android merges with the pen\'s input. Saber\'s developers aren\'t involved and aren\'t responsible for this, so please don\'t report problems with it to Saber.
